materials.title: At the dentist’s desk
materials.text:
Choose the best reply in each conversation.

1. Receptionist: Good morning. What is your name?
Child: ____

2. Receptionist: Is your appointment at ten?
Child: ____

3. Child: Where should we wait?
Receptionist: ____

4. Receptionist: Would you like a book while you wait?
Child: ____

5. Receptionist: It is your turn now. Please come with your mum.
Child: ____

questions.prompt:
Receptionist: Good morning. What is your name?
Child: ____
questions.explanation: Giving a name answers the identity request. Location/count/colour do not.

questions.prompt:
Receptionist: Is your appointment at ten?
Child: ____
options: Yes. Mum booked it for ten.
questions.explanation: Confirming the appointment time answers the question. Family/preference/ability do not.

questions.prompt:
Child: Where should we wait?
Receptionist: ____
options: Please sit on the blue seats.
questions.explanation: The seats are a waiting place. Object/origin/day count do not answer where.

questions.prompt:
Receptionist: Would you like a book while you wait?
Child: ____
options: Yes, please. This animal book looks fun.
questions.explanation: Accepting and choosing a book responds to the offer. Other replies are unrelated.

questions.prompt:
Receptionist: It is your turn now. Please come with your mum.
Child: ____
questions.explanation: Coming with Mum follows the instruction. Object/date/sighting do not.

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: Holding the corner still responds to help. Location/taste/vehicle identity do not.

questions.prompt:

options: Shall we use a shorter piece?
questions.explanation: A shorter ribbon addresses length. Shoes/age/day do not.

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

options: You’re welcome. I hope she likes it.
questions.explanation: Acknowledging thanks and a wish fit. Location/family/water do not.

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

units.title: Borrowing a ruler
units.alignmentNote: One complete six-line ordering task with the first line fixed and five positions2–6 to fill. Five scoring slots form one dialogue task, not five independent conversations. New complete communicative chain.
units.instruction: Read all six lines. Speakers A and B take turns. The first line is given. Choose position 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 for each remaining line.

materials.title: Borrowing a ruler
materials.text:
The first line is already in position 1. Put the other five lines in positions 2–6 to make one complete conversation.

(1) A: May I use your ruler, please?

(____) B: Of course. Is this short one long enough?

(____) B: That is fine. I will not need it before then.

(____) B: Then take this longer one.

(____) A: No. I need to draw a line across this large page.

(____) A: Thank you. I will bring it back after art class.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “B: Of course. Is this short one long enough?”
questions.explanation: Position2 grants the request and asks about length. The following No must answer that question.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “B: That is fine. I will not need it before then.”
questions.explanation: Position6 accepts the proposed return after art class; before then depends on the preceding return promise.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “B: Then take this longer one.”
questions.explanation: Position4 responds to the length problem with another ruler. Thanks follows receiving that solution.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “A: No. I need to draw a line across this large page.”
questions.explanation: Position3 answers the short-ruler question and explains needing a longer line, before a longer ruler is offered.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “A: Thank you. I will bring it back after art class.”
questions.explanation: Position5 thanks the lender and gives a return time. The final line refers back to that time.

materials.title: A rainy picnic
materials.text:

(____) A: No, that table is wet too.

(____) B: Good. I will bring a cloth to wipe them.

(____) B: Could we use the covered table by the hall?

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “B: Then let’s ask the teacher about eating in our classroom.”
questions.explanation: Position4 asks the teacher about the classroom after the table is rejected. She says yes follows that request.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “A: She says yes, if we clear the desks afterwards.”
questions.explanation: Position5 reports the teacher’s condition about desks. The cloth in the last line addresses cleaning them.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “A: No, that table is wet too.”
questions.explanation: Position3 says the proposed table is wet. Then in the next line introduces the alternative.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “B: Good. I will bring a cloth to wipe them.”
questions.explanation: Position6 responds to the desk-cleaning condition with a cloth; them refers to the desks.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “B: Could we use the covered table by the hall?”
questions.explanation: Position2 proposes the covered table after the rain problem. The next line rejects that specific table.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “A: Yes, my lesson finishes at half past four.”
questions.explanation: Position3 confirms five and explains the lesson end. The meeting agreement then uses that time.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “A: Which gate? The park has two.”
questions.explanation: Position5 asks which of the two gates, immediately before a distinguishing location is supplied.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “B: Would five o’clock be better?”
questions.explanation: Position2 proposes a later time to solve the four-o’clock problem. Yes answers this proposal next.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “B: The one beside the bus stop.”
questions.explanation: Position6 identifies the gate beside the bus stop and answers Which gate.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “B: Let’s meet by the park gate at five, then.”
questions.explanation: Position4 agrees time and a park-gate place. Which gate must follow that place proposal.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “A: All right. Would you like to read my copy after lunch?”
questions.explanation: Position3 agrees to keep the ending secret and offers the book. Yes in the next line accepts the offer.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “B: Yes, please. My copy is at home.”
questions.explanation: Position4 accepts the offered copy and explains why it is needed. The following line sets the loan time.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “B: Don’t tell me! I am still on page ten.”
questions.explanation: Position2 asks not to reveal the ending mentioned first. All right accepts this request in the next turn.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “A: You can keep it until tomorrow.”
questions.explanation: Position5 allows keeping the offered book until tomorrow. That in the final line refers to the extra time.

questions.prompt: What is the position of this line? “B: Thank you. That gives me time to finish.”
questions.explanation: Position6 thanks the lender for the return period, saying it gives time to finish.
